lede: MOLI is only ever mined — no pre-sale, no ICO. Swap on the chain’s own market, launch a token, cross to Ethereum and back. Nothing here asks to be believed: run a node and check every block.
livenote: Read from this node just now. Anyone with their own node arrives at the same numbers.
s1d: MetaMask or any EVM wallet. The network goes in with one click.
s2d: A Windows and Mac installer that runs in the background — or buy bMOLI with ETH.
s3d: Swap, pay a shop by QR, create a token, cross to Ethereum.
pMarket: One pool per token, two-hop routes, and MOLI’s price in reais worked out step by step, with where each number comes from.
dSwap: Molibra’s DEX: any listed pair, routed through the curve or the pool automatically.
dQuote: What a real is worth in MOLI — R$, US$, ETH, bMOLI — with live charts.
dBuy: ETH → bMOLI on Ethereum, and optionally straight to MOLI on Molibra.
dPay: A shop shows a QR with the amount and sees the payment arrive.
dPool: Add and read depth. A deposit adds depth; it never sets a price.
dBroker: The Ethereum side: WSRO, WETH and the live position.
pMemes: Each: 95% of supply on a price curve, 4% the operator’s on vesting (6-month cliff, 24 months linear) and 1% in the pool. From 26 Oct 2026 each curve’s liquidity can be withdrawn by the operator. Live price, chart and buying on the token page.
mCaramelo: The caramel street dog, Brazil’s national mascot, now on chain.
mBolso: A meme from one side of the stands.
mFazol: A meme from the other side. Same curve, same rules.
pBridge: Burning MOLI mints bMOLI on Ethereum against a proof; bMOLI sent to the vault comes back as MOLI. Fees cover the gas (and up to 0.3% on the fast bridge) — or claim it yourself, with no bridge fee.
dPonte: One click per direction; the page follows the rest. ~25 h to Ethereum, minutes back.
dFast: In minutes, from the operator’s inventory (custodial during the swap): 0.1–0.3% + the gas.
dBmoli: Burn MOLI here and mint the same amount on Ethereum against the proof.
dReturn: bMOLI → MOLI through the vault, step by step.
dSettle: Anchor a block on Ethereum and release a bridge-out against the proof.
dMine: Open the installer, paste an address (or let it make one), done.
dMiner: Watch the miner work, right in the page.
dCreate: A question or an asset. The id is derived, never chosen: nobody squats a name.
dChalk: Solve a puzzle bound to your address and receive the units expression costs.
dDocs: Register a document’s hash on chain, with a date nobody can erase.
dOut: Sign the statement that a holding is leaving. On its own it destroys nothing.
pVerify: The block format, the validation rules and replication are public. Divergence between nodes is detectable by anyone.
dScan: Any block, transaction or address, read straight out of the chain.
dStatus: Nodes, height, anchors and the network’s health.
dPaper: What the chain does — and a section listing only what is unsolved.
dSource: Apache-2.0. Clone it, run the README, compare with your own node.
dTheories: Libertarian theory and the Macrobiotic Quantum Theory, named in the genesis block.
dApi: Identity, height, activations and audit routes, as JSON.
hWallet: Any EVM wallet already speaks Molibra.
pWallet: No special client: the network answers the JSON-RPC methods an ordinary wallet calls. A public endpoint is a convenience, not the design — run your own.
headline: Money you *mine*. A chain you *check*.
hBridge: MOLI ⇄ bMOLI. *Low fees, in the open.*
hBuild: Your computer mines. *Your idea becomes a token.*
honest: **It could be worth zero. It could be worth billions. Nobody knows — not even us.** MOLI is issued by mining; its value comes only from people who want to use it. The bridge is backed by a bonded attestation, not proof of work — it is all in the white paper, including what is still missing.
